account: It is day 1 at six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. I have not yet seen today's activity, so I cannot say anything unusual is happening. Yesterday the neighbour welcomed me to dockside tea and requested an ordinary meeting at town hall today at eighteen. I agreed, and the secretary recorded it in an appointment addendum. The neighbour said the afternoon had been quiet; I do not know what today's chat will concern. The secretary reported no incoming correspondence, bills, or waiting visitors yesterday. The accounts record recorded my report of 128 emeralds in the treasury, unchanged, and no separate account papers supplied. I heard someone say the baker was carrying wheat at the bakery, which sounds consistent with ordinary bread-making, not evidence of anything unusual. My business today is to read the appointment books in the office this morning and keep the scheduled engagements: office at eight, mill inspection at ten, lunch at twelve, council letters at thirteen, tea at fifteen, and the neighbour's town-hall meeting at eighteen. The location or host for today's tea was not confirmed in what I heard.
